implementation_notes: The domain module imports nothing from an ORM: the root is a plain class over `_lines` with a tuple-returning property, value parts are `@dataclass(frozen=True)` (assignment raises FrozenInstanceError), and mapping plus transaction is a hand-written repository/mapper. Choose this when the domain must stay persistence-ignorant or the store is not relational; the invariant code is identical to the SQLAlchemy variant, only the mapping moves outside the model.
pitfalls: `tuple(self._lines)` is a shallow copy: the OrderLine objects themselves stay shared, so immutable value parts (or defensive copies) are required for the boundary to hold.
frozen=True stops attribute assignment only; a frozen part holding a list is still mutable, and `object.__setattr__` remains a documented escape hatch.
Without a session there is no change tracking: the repository must compute the child diff itself, otherwise removed lines survive as orphans and reappear on the next load.
Python exposes everything: private intent must be enforced by convention, code review and tests that construct the aggregate through its public commands only.

variants.name: SQLAlchemy-mapped aggregate (session as unit of work)
variants.implementation_notes: With SQLAlchemy the root is a mapped class whose parts are children on `relationship(..., cascade='all, delete-orphan')` - the documented setting 'for related objects which only exist as long as they are attached to their parent, and are otherwise deleted' - and the `Session` is the unit of work that flushes root and children together. Because Python has no private instance variables (only convention and accidental name mangling), the boundary is a discipline: keep `_lines`, expose a `@property` returning a tuple, and mutate only through methods. Choose this variant when the model may carry persistence metadata.
pitfalls: Name mangling is not privacy: `_lines` and even `__lines` (`order._Order__lines`) remain reachable, so the invariant holds only while every mutation goes through methods - never export the live list.
A relationship attribute is a live collection: returning it or replacing it lets callers bypass the root, and the delete-orphan cascade will delete rows for children dropped from it.
Mutating a detached instance does not flush and lazy loads raise DetachedInstanceError; the application service must own the session/transaction.
`expire_on_commit` (default true) invalidates the aggregate after commit, so touching parts afterwards triggers implicit I/O - use the returned object or configure explicitly.
